title: Multi-step shape problems: perimeter and area
canonical_examples_source: Arithmetic self-verified; method ref: NCERT Class 5/6 Maths; format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024 maths.

blocks.content: Some shape problems need two ideas at once — perimeter (the distance around) and area (the space inside). Take them one at a time. Quick words: multi-step means solving a problem by doing two or more steps one after the other.
Perimeter is the total distance around a shape. For a rectangle, add the length and width, then double it: 2 x (length + width).

steps: A rectangle is 5 cm by 3 cm.

blocks.prompt: A 5 cm by 3 cm rectangle has perimeter 2 x (5 + 3) = ___ cm
blocks.rule: Perimeter of a rectangle = 2 x (length + width).

practiceItems.prompt: perimeter of a 4 by 2 rectangle: 2 x (4 + 2)
perimeter of a square with side 5: 4 x 5
perimeter of a square with side 3

blocks.content: Area is the space inside a shape. For a rectangle, multiply length by width.

blocks.prompt: Area of a 5 cm by 3 cm rectangle = 5 x 3 = ___ square cm
blocks.explain: Area = length x width = 5 x 3 = 15 square cm.
blocks.rule: Area of a rectangle = length x width.

practiceItems.prompt: area of a square with side 5
area of a square with side 4

blocks.question: A square garden has sides of 5 m. You need fencing around it and grass inside it. One of these is 20 and one is 25 — which is which?
blocks.explain: Perimeter is the distance around: 4 sides of 5 m = 4 x 5 = 20 m of fencing. Area is the space inside: 5 x 5 = 25 square metres of grass. They measure different things, so they have different units.
blocks.rule: Perimeter is the distance around (add the sides); area is the space inside (length x width).
blocks.principle: Perimeter and area measure different things and are not interchangeable.
canonical_solution: So 20 is the perimeter and 25 is the area

rubric.look_for: matches fencing to perimeter and grass to area

misconceptions.coach: Fencing goes around (perimeter 20 m); grass fills inside (area 25 square m).

misconceptions.if: uses the same value for both
misconceptions.coach: Add sides for perimeter; multiply sides for area.

practiceItems.prompt: the perimeter of a 5 m square
the area of a 5 m square

blocks.content: Perimeter adds up all the sides; area multiplies length by width. Keep the two ideas separate and work step by step. Let's practise!
